# Bitcraft Prompt Stack Maintenance

> Origin: Generated by AI Ops via Claude on 2026-05-19. Human review: pending.

This guide keeps the Bitcraft agentic AI stack lean, inspectable, and maintainable without embedding LLM evaluation frameworks in the application repository.

## Repository Scope

Keep only low-cost static helpers in this repository:

- `.markdownlint.jsonc` for Markdown structure across `.github/`, `docs/`, and other Markdown files.
- `.vale.ini` plus `.github/vale/styles/` for prose rules, provenance checks, and narrow retired-term checks that do not conflict with governance docs.
- `mcp-server` read-only tools for repository context and quick spot checks, including `verify_architecture_readonly`.

Do not add prompt-regression frameworks, provider credentials, hosted dashboards, or benchmark datasets to this repository unless the human explicitly approves a separate evaluation project or CI integration.

## Layer Contract

Use one job per layer:

- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`: durable always-on project rules.
- `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`: file-pattern rules.
- `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md`: manually invoked workflow entrypoints.
- `.github/agents/*.agent.md`: role boundaries, tool policy, inbox protocol, and handoffs.
- `.github/skills/*/SKILL.md`: reusable procedures loaded only when relevant.
- `.github/inboxes/*/inbox.md`: active future work only, not logs or reports.
- `.github/agentic-ai/*.md`: governance, metrics, audits, model routing, and stack maintenance guidance.
- `.github/mcp/*.md` and `mcp-server/`: read-only context/tool contracts.

## Ambiguity Controls

During agentic audits or prompt edits, look for:

- Duplicate ownership: the same responsibility assigned to multiple agents without a handoff rule.
- Vague verbs: "handle", "improve", "manage", or "support" without acceptance criteria.
- Platform drift: unverified Copilot, MCP, CLI, or hook features copied from another surface.
- Prompt bloat: long procedures duplicated across prompts, agents, and skills.
- Tool mismatch: broad tool access where a narrow read/search/edit surface is enough.
- Stale routing: version-pinned model names or old provider assumptions.
- Inboxes-as-logs: completed work accumulating instead of being removed.

Resolve ambiguity by moving durable rules upward into instructions, reusable workflows sideways into skills, and one-off work downward into inboxes.

## Maintenance Loop

Use this loop for AI Ops or Agentic Audit work:

1. Inventory the changed layer: prompts, agents, skills, instructions, MCP, or docs.
2. Search for stale terms and paths (`prompt-eval`, retired CLI terms, old agent names, old folder names).
3. Run static checks: markdownlint and Vale.
4. Run architecture spot checks when backend boundaries are involved (`verify_architecture_readonly`, then tests/CI if enforcing).
5. Record material decisions in `FRAMEWORK_REVIEW.md`; create inbox items only for future action.
6. Keep evaluation claims grounded in repository evidence, official docs, or clearly marked assumptions.

## Static Checks

Recommended local commands from the repository root:

```powershell
npx markdownlint-cli2 --config .markdownlint.jsonc ".github/**/*.md" "docs/**/*.md" "*.md"
vale --config .vale.ini .github docs *.md
```

These checks are cheap and deterministic. They do not measure prompt effectiveness; they only catch structure, prose, and governance drift.

## Architecture Validation

The current built-in helper is `verify_architecture_readonly` in `mcp-server/server.py`. It reports obvious Clean Architecture boundary violations in `Bitcraft.Domain` and `Bitcraft.Application`.

For enforceable architecture validation, create a separate backend work item and evaluate one of these routes:

- Architecture tests in `tests/` using a .NET architecture-testing library.
- Roslyn analyzer rules for forbidden references or namespace boundaries.
- Commercial architecture analysis if the team wants dashboards and trend history.

Do not treat the MCP spot check as CI enforcement.

## External Prompt Evaluation Options

If Bitcraft later needs measured prompt or agent quality, keep it outside this application repo unless explicitly approved.

| Option | Fit | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Promptfoo | Local prompt matrix testing, model comparison, red-team experiments. | Good for a separate `bitcraft-agent-evals` repo or temporary local lab. No project dependency needed. |
| LangSmith | Datasets, experiments, tracing, human review queues, offline and online evals. | Strong when Bitcraft needs trace-backed AI application evaluation. |
| Braintrust | Prompt playgrounds, immutable experiments, CI regression checks, production scoring. | Strong for collaborative evaluation workflows and pull-request quality gates. |
| Langfuse | Prompt management, observability, datasets, live evaluators. | Strong if the tutor runtime needs trace observability and prompt version management. |
| DeepEval | Local Python evals, agent/RAG metrics, CI-friendly test cases. | Already belongs near the Python sidecar benchmark workflow; do not duplicate it in `.github`. |

Suggested future path: create a separate evaluation project only after the team has 10-20 curated examples of successful and failed agent outputs. Start with human-reviewed examples before adding LLM-as-judge scoring.

## GitHub Docs Check

Checked on 2026-05-19 with `fetch_webpage`:

- GitHub Copilot customization cheat sheet lists custom instructions, prompt files, custom agents, subagents, agent skills, hooks, and MCP servers as customization primitives.
- GitHub custom-instructions support confirms VS Code support for `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/instructions/**/*.instructions.md`, and `AGENTS.md`-style agent instructions.
- GitHub MCP docs confirm MCP tools are invoked through Agent mode and may require additional permissions.
- No GitHub doc checked here requires prompt-evaluation tooling inside the repository.

Open ambiguity: GitHub docs describe custom agents as `.github/agents/AGENT-NAME.md`, while Bitcraft currently uses `.github/agents/*.agent.md` per the active VS Code convention in this repository. Do not rename the agent files without validating the active Copilot client and updating all references in one migration.
